Training the next generation of scientists and clinicians is part of what this lab is for. We teach the way we do research: at the bench, with real experiments that can fail, with the published data the field actually argues about, and with the tools scientists use today, including language models, used critically and logged when they are wrong.

Our courses are built in the open. The material lives in public repositories, students work from the same files we edit, and anyone is welcome to read along or send input.

::: {.callout-warning title="Under construction"}
The Blockrophage course runs for the first time in spring 2027 and is being built in the open. Interested students are welcome to apply and to give input through the [contact page](contact.qmd) or the [issues on GitHub](https://github.com/TizzuLab/blockrophage-course/issues). **Please do not use these protocols in the lab yet.** Values are unverified until this notice is gone.
:::

## Blockrophage course

**Macrophage Biology: in vitro, in vivo, in silico.** A four-week block course for D-BIOL, ETH Zürich, Spring Semester 2027. Students build the textbook M1/M2 picture of macrophages with their own hands in a dish, then test it against real tissue macrophages in a published single-cell dataset. It does not survive intact; the field made the same discovery ten years ago.

The repository is the course: the script, the schedule, every protocol, the background reading, the lecture slides and the analysis code, with a single-file companion students can hand to the language model of their choice.

### Schedule at a glance

Four weeks, one drawing each. Two groups at the bench in the morning and two at the keyboard, swapped after lunch; the dark cells are fixed, everything else is drawn by each group with its supervisor on the first afternoon.
